sabians.name: The Sabians
sabians.title: The Sabians
sabians.dict: Named three times beside the Jews and the Christians (2:62, 5:69, 22:17). Who they were is not certain; the name has been applied to several groups.

salih.name: Salih
salih.title: Salih
salih.dict: The messenger sent to Thamud, a people who carved their houses out of the mountains. He brings them a she-camel as a sign and tells them to let her drink; they hamstring her and are destroyed (7:73-79, 11:61-68, 26:141-158). He has no counterpart in the Bible.

samiri.name: The Samiri
samiri.title: The Samiri
samiri.dict: The man who leads the Children of Israel astray while Moses is on the mountain, and makes the calf that lows (20:85-97). Moses condemns him to say "No contact" all his life. The Quran gives him no other name.

satan.name: Satan
satan.title: Satan (Iblis)
satan.dict: Iblis refuses to bow to Adam: "I am better than he; You created me from fire, and You created him from mud" (7:12). He "was of the jinn" (18:50). Cast out, he is given respite until the Day of Resurrection and vows to mislead Adam's children, but has no authority over God's sincere servants (15:39-42). As Satan he whispers to Adam and his wife, and is "to man an open enemy" (17:53).

saul.name: Saul
saul.title: Saul (Talut)
saul.dict: The king appointed for the Children of Israel when they ask their prophet for one. He tests his troops at a river, and only a few stay with him to face Goliath (2:246-249).

shuayb.name: Shuayb
shuayb.title: Shuayb
shuayb.dict: The messenger sent to Midian and to the people of the Woods. He tells them to give full measure and weight and not to cheat; they threaten to drive him out and are destroyed (7:85-93, 11:84-95, 26:176-189). Later tradition often identifies him with Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses; the Quran does not.

solomon.name: Solomon
solomon.title: Solomon (Sulayman)
solomon.dict: David's heir, taught the speech of birds, with the wind, the jinn and the birds at his command (27:15-17, 34:12-13, 38:36-38). He overhears an ant, and brings the queen of Sheba to faith (27:18-44). "It was not Solomon who disbelieved" (2:102): the Quran calls him a prophet and a penitent servant, and does not say that he turned to other gods.
